subject: science
passage: The purple frog of India's Western Ghats was not formally described by scientists until 2003, although people in the region had long known it. Its late recognition reflects its habits more than its rarity: the frog spends most of the year underground, where it feeds mainly on termites with its narrow, pointed snout, and it surfaces for only a few weeks during the monsoon to breed in temporary streams. Genetic studies indicate that its closest living relatives are small frogs found only in the Seychelles, islands in the Indian Ocean. The two lineages are thought to have diverged long ago, when India and the Seychelles were still joined as parts of the ancient supercontinent Gondwana.
stem: Based on the text, what is the main reason the purple frog went unrecognized by scientists for so long?

choices.A: It is so rare that few people in the Western Ghats had ever encountered it.
choices.B: It lives underground for most of the year and comes to the surface only briefly.
choices.C: Its closest living relatives are found only on islands in the Indian Ocean.
choices.D: It feeds almost entirely on termites, a food that few other kinds of frogs will eat.

explanation.why: The second sentence answers the question: the frog's late recognition "reflects its habits more than its rarity," and the colon introduces those habits, chiefly that it stays underground most of the year and surfaces "for only a few weeks." A frog that is seldom above ground is easy for scientists to miss.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The text says the late recognition reflects habits "more than its rarity" and that local people "had long known it."
explanation.B: Correct. This restates the habits the text gives as the reason: life underground with only brief appearances.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is true according to the text, but it concerns the frog's ancestry, not why scientists overlooked it.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The text says it feeds mainly on termites but never compares its diet with other frogs or links diet to its late discovery.
